nodes.d: The Preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem, examines life under the sun and declares that all is vanity, yet counsels the fear of God and keeping his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment (12:13-14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the Preacher’s repeated word “vanity” and his conclusion in chapter 12?
ev: Say who speaks in Ecclesiastes and state the closing conclusion in 12:13-14.

nodes.t: All is vanity: the weariness of life under the sun
nodes.d: The Preacher says all is vanity, that one generation goes and another comes while the earth abides, that the sun and wind keep returning, that there is nothing new, and that he gave his heart to know wisdom and found it vexation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the Preacher means by “under the sun” in chapter 1?
ev: Read 1:2-11 and list the cycles named.
Say what the Preacher concludes in 1:14.

nodes.t: Pleasure, wealth and labour are vanity
nodes.d: The Preacher tests pleasure, great works, gardens and riches, then sees that the wise and the fool share one event, that he must leave his labour to another, and says enjoying good in labour is from God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the Preacher tried in chapter 2 and what he concluded?
ev: List what the Preacher tried in 2:1-10 and his verdict in 2:11.
Read 2:24-26 and state what comes from the hand of God.

nodes.d: The Preacher says there is a season for every purpose, from birth and death to weeping and laughing, that God made everything beautiful in its time and put eternity in men’s hearts yet no man can find out his work, and that all go to the dust.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 and explain what 3:11 adds?
ev: Read 3:1-8 and list four pairs.
Read 3:11 and 3:14 and say what the Preacher says about God’s work.

nodes.t: Oppression, envy and two are better than one
nodes.d: The Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed with no comforter, that toil arises from envy, that a man alone has no second, and that two are better than one and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why two are better than one according to Ecclesiastes 4:9-12?
ev: Read 4:9-12 and list the reasons two are better than one.

nodes.t: Guard your step in God’s house; the vanity of riches
nodes.d: The Preacher says to keep your foot when going to the house of God, not to be hasty with the mouth or with vows, and that he who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; enjoying one’s labour is a gift of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 5:1-7 says about speaking to God?
ev: Read 5:1-7 and list the instructions about worship and vows.
Read 5:10-15 and state what is said about loving riches.

nodes.t: Wealth without enjoyment; what is man the better?
nodes.d: The Preacher describes a man to whom God gives riches but not the power to eat of them, says a stillborn child has more rest, and asks who knows what is good for man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize the “evil” the Preacher sees in Ecclesiastes 6:1-2?
ev: Say what evil the Preacher describes in 6:1-2 and what question he asks in 6:11-12.

nodes.t: Better is the house of mourning; wisdom and its limits
nodes.d: The Preacher gathers sayings that the house of mourning is better than feasting, the rebuke of the wise better than the song of fools, and the end of a thing better than its beginning, notes there is not a just man who sins not, and says wisdom is far from him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three “better” sayings from Ecclesiastes 7 and read what 7:20 says?
ev: Find the “better than” sayings in chapter 7 and say what each prefers.
Read 7:20 and 7:29.

nodes.t: Obey the king; the work of God cannot be found out
nodes.d: The Preacher counsels keeping the king’s commandment, observes that sentence against evil is not carried out speedily, that the righteous sometimes get what the wicked deserve, and that man cannot find out the work of God under the sun.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what troubles the Preacher in Ecclesiastes 8:14?
ev: Read 8:11-14 and state what puzzles the Preacher.
Read 8:17.

nodes.t: One event comes to all; enjoy life; time and chance
nodes.d: The Preacher says the same event comes to the righteous and the wicked, that the living know they shall die, tells his reader to eat and drink with joy and enjoy life with the wife he loves, and says the race is not always to the swift and wisdom is better than weapons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 9:11 says about outcomes?
ev: Read 9:7-10 and list the counsel given.
Read 9:11-12 and say what the Preacher observes.

nodes.t: Dead flies and fools: sayings on folly and wisdom
nodes.d: Sayings say dead flies spoil ointment, that he who digs a pit may fall into it, that a fool is full of words, and that one should not curse the king, even in thought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain one saying about folly from Ecclesiastes 10?
ev: Find three sayings in chapter 10 about the fool and say what harm each describes.

nodes.t: Cast your bread on the waters; remember your Creator
nodes.d: The Preacher tells men to give a portion and sow in the morning since they cannot know the work of God, to rejoice in their youth yet know that God will bring them to judgment, and to remember their Creator before the evil days come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 12:1 and explain what it tells the young to do?
ev: Read 11:9-12:1 and say what is said about youth.
List the images of old age in 12:1-7.

nodes.t: The conclusion: fear God and keep his commandments
nodes.d: The Preacher sought out acceptable words, says the words of the wise are as goads and nails given by one Shepherd, warns that of making many books there is no end, and concludes that the whole duty of man is to fear God and keep his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the conclusion of Ecclesiastes in 12:13-14 in their own words?
ev: Read 12:13-14 and state the conclusion.
